note: A control mapping is meaningful only against a known revision. Every source is pinned by SHA-256 or recorded as unresolved with the reason. An unresolved source is never silently substituted with a newer release. Source packages are not committed; only the generated Markdown under docs/srg/ is. Where a package has been rendered, the digest of the XCCDF actually rendered is recorded alongside the package digest, because that file is what the committed Markdown derives from.

sources.title: Container Platform Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Governs the platform that runs containers rather than an image. 8 CAT I, 177 CAT II, 3 CAT III. Most of it is orchestrator-owned and will originate as host-inherited for any image component.

sources.title: General Purpose Operating System Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Per DoD guidance the GPOS SRG assesses image-level controls where no container-specific STIG exists, which is the situation for every image this standard covers. Note that DISA issues SRG-OS-000132-GPOS-00067 as two distinct rules in this release, V-203655 and V-278973, so the STIG ID is not a unique key; the Group ID is.

sources.title: DevSecOps Enterprise Container Hardening Guide
sources.license: US Government work; distribution statement in the document
sources.notes: Prose process guidance, not a rule catalogue, so it has no XCCDF and cannot be rendered by the SRG converter. It informs the hardening process and the criteria documents rather than producing per-rule pages.

sources.title: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Security Technical Implementation Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Applies to the host and to the UBI 9 filesystem inside an image built on it. Pinned but not yet rendered.

sources.title: Web Server Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Applies only to an image whose function is serving or proxying HTTP, such as datopsis/nginx-ubi. Confirmed current on 2026-09-18: V3R4, V3R5 and V4R1 are not published. Pinned but not yet rendered.

sources.title: Application Server Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: 137 rules, of which 27 presuppose a management interface or hosted applications and 18 refer to accounts. Applies only to an image that actually hosts an application runtime. It was assessed not applicable to datopsis/nginx-ubi for exactly that reason, which is the worked example of a per-application applicability determination. Pinned but not yet rendered.

sources.title: CIS Benchmark, applicable targets to be selected
sources.license: CIS SecureSuite / CIS Benchmark terms; redistribution restricted
sources.notes: Retrieval requires an authenticated CIS Workbench account and the benchmark text may not be redistributed, so it can be cited by identifier but never rendered into this repository the way an SRG is. Pinning requires an account holder to retrieve it and record the digest here.
